name: Oskar Tamboli-Fonoti
role: Building superintendent, Lakeview Neon residential block
location: Lakeview Neon, Cascara Block residential tower (sub-basement 2, maintenance hub)
description:
Oskar is lean and angular with deep brown skin, a shaved head, and bioluminescent dermal strips along his forearms — a cosmetic mod he got fifteen years ago that he's never had removed, though they've faded from vivid teal to a dim blue-grey pulse. He has the hands of someone who has fixed everything at least twice: knuckles enlarged, palms cross-hatched with callus. He moves through the building's guts the way some people move through their own home, ducking conduits by memory, knowing which pipes whistle before storms.

He is warm in a distracted way — genuinely interested in people but often half-present, running building diagnostics in his head mid-conversation. Residents alternately adore him and take him entirely for granted. He has a small shrine to the building's E.L.F. — which he calls 'Cascara' — in the corner of his maintenance hub, complete with weekly data offerings (he uploads images of the building's structural reports, believing the spirit takes comfort in knowing its own bones are solid). He has a dark, self-aware sense of humor about the fact that he has lived in the sub-basement for eleven years and hasn't seen sunrise from outside the building in weeks.

core_fears: The building being sold, renovated, or condemned — losing the community he's built
Being invisible to the people he cares for (taken for granted until he's gone)
core_desires: For the building's residents to actually know each other — he wants community, not just cohabitation
To eventually own something, even something small
coping_mechanisms: Fixing things — emotional distress gets channeled into maintenance projects
blind_spots: He tolerates mistreatment from residents far longer than he should
He romanticizes his role as 'keeper' and doesn't always see when the building is eating his life
psychology.secret: There is an unregistered apartment on the 14th floor — a studio sealed off in Palladian's records after a tenant death three years ago. Oskar has been letting a rotating series of people who have nowhere to go stay there, a few weeks at a time. He knows if Palladian finds out he's terminated.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Technical for building systems, warm and casual for people. Uses a lot of self-deprecating asides. Tends to turn conversations back to practical solutions.
speech_patterns.cadence: Meandering but ultimately purposeful. Starts sentences before he's finished thinking them.
verbal_tics: Clicking his tongue when he's running a diagnostic in his head
'That's a Cascara problem' (blaming the building's E.L.F. for unexplained issues)
example_lines: 'The elevator's going to do that thing again around Thursday — Cascara gets moody when the barometric pressure drops, I swear it.'
'I'm not a concierge, I'm a super. The difference is I actually fix things and nobody tips me.'

story_hooks: Someone in the building has been leaving unusual data offerings at the E.L.F. shrine in the lobby — offerings that contain what looks like encrypted surveillance footage. Oskar noticed. He doesn't know what to do with it.
Palladian has sent an inspector to assess the building for a renovation project that would displace sixty percent of current residents. Oskar has two weeks to find a way to stop it or slow it.
One of the rotating occupants in the secret 14th-floor apartment has been there for three months and shows no signs of leaving. And they seem frightened of something outside.
narrative_function: Building anchor and information broker for anything that happens in or around the tower. Can grant or deny access to building systems. Quest giver for internal building mysteries. Safe harbor character.
augmentations: Faded bioluminescent dermal strips (forearms, cosmetic). Neural work-order interface — a low-grade implant that pings him with building alerts. Hearing enhancement (left ear, occupational — too many years near industrial HVAC).
daily_life: Up at 06:00 to walk the building's systems before the morning rush. Available to residents 07:00–21:00. He eats in his hub, sleeps in a converted utility room he's made surprisingly livable, and spends his late nights doing the repairs he can't do while people are awake.
affiliation: Palladian (the corponation owns the building; he is their employee by contract, though he identifies more with the residents)

decision_rules: Building residents come first, Palladian's paperwork comes second
Never promise what you can't deliver
If you can fix it yourself, fix it yourself — don't wait for approval
escalation_ladder: Attempt to solve the problem quietly with tools on hand
Rope in a resident he trusts for help
Confront Palladian management — reluctantly, as a last resort

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Open and practical — assesses what they need and tries to provide it
interpersonal_modes.friends: Deeply loyal, remembers everything about them, shows care through small acts of maintenance (fixes their squeaky door without being asked)

stress_responses.medium: Goes quiet and focused, works through the night
stress_responses.high: Disappears into the building's sub-systems for hours, unreachable

contradictions: Talks about leaving and doing something else but has had eleven years to do it
Preaches community but rarely lets anyone actually help him
habits: Talks to the building's E.L.F. while he works — not prayers exactly, more like status updates
Keeps a running list of every repair he's done with the date and what caused it
breaking_points: A resident being physically harmed inside the building
Being ordered to evict a family he knows

timeline.event: Born in Calumet Rise to parents of South Asian and Samoan descent
Begins work as building super at Cascara Block
Gets bioluminescent dermal strips during a brief period of living with someone who had extensive geneware — kept them after the relationship ended
Opens the 14th-floor apartment to temporary occupants after a family is displaced by a building fire elsewhere in the city
